findings.reason: s6's root-cause sentence and width-writer design must be marked superseded by s14's controller, or an implementer builds the very memory rule that ran the width to the cap.
findings.text: §6 opens "What binds is KV occupancy, not a width knee" and prescribes a width writer that sets width "from pool tokens × an occupancy target ÷ a slowly moving context estimate"; §6's own landed note (s6) records that this occupancy rule "does not find a boundary; it runs out of populated bins" and returns the engine cap, and §14 (s14) measures the knee at about 12 running with KV ≈0.2–0.3 and states "the collapse tracks the running count, not the working set … the gate width is the lever", replacing the memory rule with a throughput controller. A node dispatched on s6 would build the occupancy÷context rule that s14 identifies as the defect.

findings.reason: a coordinator reading the node table dispatches a node to redo work already committed, and the section's landed state is misreported.
findings.text: s21 declares itself "implementable" and its node table lists the "One occupancy target" node as outstanding, but that node is already in the tree: lane.py:43 reads `DEFAULT_OCCUPANCY_TARGET = 0.90` with the exact corrected comment s21 asks for, router.py:162 reads `DEFAULT_AUTO_OCCUPANCY_TARGET = LaneCapacity.OCCUPANCY_TARGET`, and the change landed as commit ca4ee22b ("fix(agent-lane): read one occupancy target in the estimator and the router", 2026-09-29).

findings.reason: without a declared negative control the node's gate can pass on a rule that never fires, and adding one changes what the node must produce.
findings.text: the router node's done-when lists fixture tests (fair-share formula, unattributed session, 200 s horizon, congested clamp) but names no negative control, unlike its sibling sections; the fair-share rule is exactly the kind of arithmetic a mutation must be shown to break.

findings.reason: splitting it into two nodes lets each change pass or fail on its own gate rather than bundling a stop-mechanism verdict with a drain-refresh verdict.
findings.text: the section carries two independently testable changes to cli.py/slurm.py (a signal-then-wait serve stop with a fallback flag, and a refusal to cancel when every replacement-hosting node is DRAIN/DRAINING) under one done-when, so the node cannot be closed on a single verdict.
